newsitem.title: USA: Honda to build $30 mln ATV plant.
newsitem.headline: Honda to build $30 mln ATV plant.

text.p: Honda Motor Co Ltd said Monday it will construct a $30 million manufacturing plant near here for the production of four-wheel all-terrain vehicles (ATVs).
The new company, Honda of South Carolina Mfg, a subsidiary of American Honda Motor Co, will begin production in fall 1998 with an annual production capacity of 100,000 units.
The company will employ 300 in the fall of 1998 and will have 600 at full production.
The announcement from Honda had been expected.
Honda said it will build the 175,000-square-foot plant on a 500-acre site southwest of Florence, near the community of Timmonsville. This will be Honda's 10th manufacturing plant in North America.

Over the past six years, Honda said, the U.S. ATV market has doubled from 150,000 units in 1991 to more than 300,000 in 1996. Honda holds about 30 percent of the market, including sales of approximately 100,000 in 1996. Almost half of Honda's sales come in 15 states within the Sun Belt region.

"Demand for ATVs and motorcycles continues to grow," John Petas, senior vice president of the American Honda Motorcycle Division, Honda's sales arm for ATVs, said in a statement. "This new plant makes us even more excited about the future. It will give us flexibility to meet the growing needs of our customers in America and other global markets."

Honda has manufactured ATVs at its Honda of America Mfg. Motorcycle Plant in Marysville, Ohio, since 1989. Honda produces four ATV models exclusively in the U.S. -- the FourTrax 400, FourTrax 300, FourTrax 300 4x4 and the FourTrax 250 Recon.
